cards.title: What does attention compute?
cards.summary: Attention mixes value vectors weighted by the similarity of queries and keys.

cards.title: Why does a CPU cache speed up programs?
cards.summary: Caches keep recently used memory close to the core, exploiting locality.

cards.title: What parts make up a VLM?
cards.summary: A vision encoder turns images into vectors and a language model reasons over them with text.

cards.title: How does stochastic gradient descent update weights?
cards.summary: It steps against the gradient of the loss computed on a small batch.

cards.title: What does a tokenizer do?
cards.summary: It splits text into subword units and maps them to integer ids.

queries.title: Why scale attention scores by sqrt(d)?
queries.summary: Scaling keeps softmax over query-key scores from saturating.

queries.title: What is multi-head attention?
queries.summary: Several attention heads attend to different subspaces in parallel.

queries.title: What is a projector in a VLM?
queries.summary: A projector maps vision features into the language model's embedding space.

queries.title: What is cache locality?
queries.summary: Programs reuse nearby memory soon, so caches hit often.

queries.title: What is the learning rate?
queries.summary: The step size that scales each gradient update.

queries.title: What is byte-pair encoding?
queries.summary: BPE merges frequent symbol pairs to build a subword vocabulary.
